speaker: Doctor
text: Good morning, I see you have been feeling unwell with fever and confusion for the past two days. To understand the cause of your altered mentation, can you tell me if you have any severe headaches, neck stiffness, or a recent history of insect bites?

speaker: Patient
text: 22-year-old male. The patient presents with a 2-day history of fever and altered mentation, reporting fever without chills and rigors. He denies sore throat, abdominal pain, headache, loose stool, burning micturition, or seizures. Has a history of tics and is currently taking haloperidol.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for the details. Given your history of tics and current use of haloperidol, does the altered mentation involve new onset confusion, agitation, or involuntary movements, and when did you last take your medication?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Fever and altered mentation. I also have Profuse sweating, Generalized rigidity, Confusion and disorientation, Ability to move all limbs, Normal deep tendon reflexes with bilateral downgoing plantar responses.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Neuroleptic Malignant Syndrome (NMS) secondary to haloperidol use.

REQUEST TEST: Creatine_Kinase, Lactate_Dehydrogenase, Electrolytes, CBC, Liver_Function_Tests.
REQUEST IMAGES: None required at this stage.
